# Results — Study 463 (Bear-Flag)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a bear
flag forecasts continuation: after a sharp drop (the pole) and a small up-sloping consolidation
(the flag), price breaks down and the second leg down follows** — encoded as a mechanical rule.
A pole is a fall of ≥ 6% (log) over a 10-bar lookback; the flag is a 7-bar *up-sloping*
consolidation retracing at most 60% of the pole; a **short** fires on the first close below the
flag's lower trendline, entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the
forward 5/10/20/60-day return **of the short** (a continued drop is a profit). Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **156** mechanical bear-flag breakdowns pooled across the 5 tapes |
| Timing / costs | pole ≥ 6% over 10 bars; flag = 7-bar up-slope (≤ 60% retrace); short on the first close below the lower flag line; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per breakdown |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument continuation study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects
> only the drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — breakdown-short vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

Everything is on the **short side** (the bear-flag trade): a *positive* number means the short
made money (price continued down). One-sample *t* against zero is misleading on a drifting tape;
the **Welch breakdown-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = breakdown − random.

| horizon | n | breakdown | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (brk−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 156 | −57.5 bps | 46% | −1.92 | −10.3 bps | **−47.2 bps** | −59.5 bps | −1.24 | 0.218 |
| 10-day | 155 | −57.3 bps | 41% | −1.55 | −53.6 bps | **−3.7 bps** | −59.3 bps | −0.07 | 0.944 |
| 20-day | 155 | −98.2 bps | 47% | −1.65 | −33.1 bps | **−65.1 bps** | −100.2 bps | −1.04 | 0.299 |
| 60-day | 153 | −303.2 bps | 29% | −3.39 | −118.9 bps | **−184.2 bps** | −305.2 bps | −1.90 | 0.059 |

Read it carefully. The bear-flag **short loses money at every horizon** (−57 / −57 / −98 / −303
bps): after the so-called continuation breakdown, price more often **rises**, so the short bleeds
— and the bleed *worsens* with horizon, exactly the signature of shorting an upward-drifting
index. Worse for the believer, the breakdown-short is **worse than shorting on random days** at
every horizon (Δ = −47.2 / −3.7 / −65.1 / −184.2 bps). The breakdown-minus-random difference
**never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (max |Welch *t*| = 1.90 at 60 days, *p* = 0.059) — and
in the *wrong* direction for the believer. The flag does not forecast continuation; if anything,
the breakdown marks a local bottom.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — no continuation anywhere

| ticker | entries | breakdown | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (brk−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 27 | +73.9 bps | +0.56 | −39.3 bps | **+113.2 bps** |
| QQQ | 31 | −177.3 bps | −1.63 | −88.2 bps | **−89.1 bps** |
| IWM | 46 | −70.3 bps | −0.80 | −2.7 bps | **−67.6 bps** |
| DIA | 20 | −141.2 bps | −0.68 | −33.7 bps | **−107.4 bps** |
| GLD | 32 | −182.4 bps | −1.35 | −1.5 bps | **−180.9 bps** |

Only **SPY** shows a positive breakdown-short (and a positive delta), on just 27 trades and at
*t* = +0.56 — noise. In 4 of 5 names the breakdown-short *loses* and *underperforms* a random
short. No coherent cross-sectional continuation — the opposite of what the pattern promises.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the flag, nothing changes

The decisive "does the flag's geometry matter?" test: keep the **pole** filter and the same
epoch, but replace the flag's defining *up-sloping* slope test with a per-bar coin, so which
bars count as "flags" is geometric nonsense. If the breakdown short genuinely depended on the
flag's structure, the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | observed breakdown 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-flag breakdown | +73.9 bps | **0.323** | 500 |

**32% of scrambled-flag breakdowns match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.323). The specific
up-sloping-flag geometry carries no information — coin-flipped flags do as well. "The flag
forecasts continuation" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real continuation

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* post-breakdown continuation (knob `edge`), the same
breakdown-short rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat (in fact negative) real-tape result
is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | breakdown | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no continuation) | 73 | +36.5 bps | 49% | +0.67 |
| **0.80** (real planted continuation) | 100 | +511.5 bps | 87% | **+10.74** |

With no planted continuation the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive, 49% win); a real
planted continuation lights up at *t* = +10.74 with an 87% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The bear-flag breakdown-short does **not** beat a drift-matched random
  short — it is *worse* at every horizon (breakdown − random = −47.2 / −3.7 / −65.1 / −184.2 bps
  at 5/10/20/60 days; the Welch *t* never clears 2, max magnitude −1.90 at 60 days, *p* = 0.059,
  and in the believer's-*wrong* direction). The short itself simply loses to the index's upward
  drift. There is no continuation edge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "continuation" never materializes; the short bleeds the equity
  drift and costs only deepen the hole. Nothing to deploy and nothing to scale — there is no
  edge, only negative carry.
- **"Does the flag forecast continuation"? — BUSTED.** The shuffled-flag placebo leaves the
  result intact (*p* = 0.323): coin-flipped flags do as well as the real geometry, so the
  up-sloping flag carries no forecasting information. The bear flag is a descriptive after-the-
  fact label, not a forecasting pattern.
